section_title: How does everyone reach shore when the ship breaks apart?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 39 When daylight came, they did not recognize the land, but they sighted a bay with a sandy beach, where they decided to run the ship aground if they could. 40 Cutting away the anchors, they left them in the sea as they loosened the ropes that held the rudders. Then they hoisted the foresail to the wind and made for the beach. 41 But the ship struck a sandbar and ran aground. The bow stuck fast and would not move, and the stern was being broken up by the pounding of the waves. 42 The soldiers planned to kill the prisoners so none of them could swim to freedom. 43 But the centurion, wanting to spare Paul’s life, thwarted their plan. He commanded those who could swim to jump overboard first and get to land. 44 The rest were to follow on planks and various parts of the ship. In this way everyone was brought safely to land.

context_lines: At daylight the crew sees an unfamiliar bay with a sandy beach and tries to run the ship onto it. They abandon the anchors, free the rudders and raise the foresail. But the ship strikes a sandbar: its bow sticks fast, and the waves begin breaking the stern apart.

The soldiers plan to kill the prisoners to prevent any escaping. Julius, wanting to spare Paul’s life, stops that plan. He orders those who can swim to go first, with the others following on planks and pieces of the ship. Everyone reaches land safely.

The rescue includes both threatened dangers: the sea and the soldiers’ proposed action. Luke reports the centurion’s desire to preserve Paul, but does not say that Julius has become a Christian or give the final destination and sentence of each prisoner.
common_interpretation_lines: Christians commonly read the outcome as the fulfillment of the assurance that no life would be lost even though the ship would be. Human decisions remain part of that outcome: the crew’s effort, Julius’s intervention, swimming and floating on wreckage all belong to the account of everyone reaching shore.
god_plan_lines: The preservation promised in [Acts 27:22–26](https://biblehub.com/bsb/acts/27.htm) has now taken a concrete form: the ship is lost, and the people live. This keeps Paul on the way toward the testimony in Rome promised in [Acts 23:11](https://biblehub.com/bsb/acts/23.htm). The wreck has not ended that commission.

The next chapter identifies the island as Malta and describes hospitality and healing there. The route to one destination opens another setting for God’s care along the way. The story’s value is greater than a successful arrival for one traveler; the lives of the people around him also matter.
